_comment: CANONICAL permission policy for ALL THREE tools (Claude Code, Grok, OpenCode).
Edit ONLY here, then run `bash ~/.agents/setup.sh`. Never hand-edit the per-tool copies.
setup.sh replaces generated permission buckets from this file so revocations propagate; other config survives:
[5b] Claude   -> ~/.claude/settings.json            permissions.allow / permissions.ask / permissions.deny
[5c] Grok     -> ~/.grok/config.toml [permission]   allow / ask / deny                    (verbatim rules)
[5d] OpenCode -> ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc  permission.bash map                   (Bash(X) -> "X": allow|ask|deny)
Rule syntax below is Claude-native. Grok/OpenCode entries are derived from enforceable Bash(...) rules;
non-Bash rules (Skill(...) etc.) are Claude-only. OpenCode gets a managed catch-all: allow when
bash_without_prompt=true, otherwise ask. Specific canonical allow/ask/deny rules are written after it.
Allow entries run WITHOUT a prompt; ask entries prompt; deny entries block. Unmatched Bash asks by default.
Deliberately absent from allow: rm, sudo, curl/wget, git push, package installs, chmod/chown, dd, mv.
Also absent on purpose: xargs -I / sh -c / bash -c / npx — they run an arbitrary inner command, so
allowing them would launder every rule here. 'sed *' IS allowed and covers in-place 'sed -i' writes;
that is intended (edits are prompt-free anyway, see defaults.edit_without_prompt).
Exception: `bash ~/.agents/sync.sh` is allowlisted. It is the ONLY no-prompt path to a push, and it
can only push signed main commits from the ~/.agents repo root after strict PASS with zero warnings. Generic `git push`
still prompts in every repo, including that one.
Matching notes: wrappers timeout/time/nice/nohup/stdbuf/command/builtin/bare-xargs are stripped before
matching, so 'Bash(pytest *)' already covers 'timeout 900 pytest -q'. Interpreter PATHS are not
normalized, hence the explicit .venv/venv entries below. Heredocs whose body mixes braces with quotes
(Python f-strings) are flagged 'expansion obfuscation' and prompt regardless of any rule here — write
the script to a scratchpad file and run the file instead (see AGENTS.md).
COMPOUND COMMANDS: a pipeline/;/&&-chain is approved only if EVERY segment matches a rule. One stray
'lscpu' in a ten-part probe prompts for the whole line — hence the bare forms next to the '* ' forms.
Tool-agnostic autonomy defaults. setup.sh translates each key per tool, verify.sh checks all three.
edit_without_prompt: writing/creating files needs no prompt.
claude   -> used only when bash_without_prompt is false: defaultMode = "acceptEdits"
grok     -> [ui] permission_mode = "acceptEdits"
opencode -> permission.edit = "allow"
bash_without_prompt: NO bash permission prompts. Required for Claude — allowlist alone cannot
kill hard-coded safety prompts (cd+write path-bypass, cd+git untrusted-hooks, parse verdicts).
claude   -> permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions" (takes precedence over acceptEdits)
grok     -> [ui] permission_mode = "always-approve"
opencode -> permission.bash catch-all "*" = "allow" (specific rules still written later)
With bash_without_prompt true, Claude ask/deny lists are best-effort only — bypass skips checks.
Current policy keeps edit_without_prompt=true and bash_without_prompt=false: edits are accepted,
canonical safe commands run silently, and unmatched Bash (including generic git push) asks.
